$comment: Shared-patch baseline (U-L3-01). Read by script/check-shared-patches.ts and script/check-opencode-annotations.ts. Each shared upstream file that Kilo adds or changes needs an entry: rung (3 = seam patch, 4 = feature patch) and the missing seam. `unmarked` allows lines without markers and states why. Raise a limit only in the PR that adds the patch, and lower it when a patch goes away.

packages/cli/src/commands/commands.ts.seam: Optional full-TUI --model/-m argument, passed to the existing TUI Args.model selector. The CLI command specification is closed and has no host extension for root parameters; no default changes when omitted. Two generic lines across the root specification and default handler replace a custom argument parser or a second host command mirror.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/defau.seam: Pass the optional model flag into the existing TUI Args.model input. The root handler's private run() options cannot be supplied by the server host or a TUI plugin. Omitted input preserves the upstream behavior.

.github/actions/setup-bun/action.yml.seam: Windows CI setup: exclude the workspace, temp and Bun directories from Defender real-time scanning before the install. Carried over from v1 (`main`). The Windows Bun cache skip that Kilo also carried is upstream since v2.0.31 (anomalyco/opencode#55866). No seam: the composite action has no input to run a step before the install, and every job that installs dependencies uses it.

.github/workflows/check.yml.seam: CI triggers and gates: run `check` on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`) and for every pull request, so stacked v2 PRs that target another PR branch are checked; skip `lint:changed` on upstream sync PRs (branch `sync-v*`), whose changed files are upstream's and fail upstream's lint too. No seam: workflow triggers and step conditions cannot be extended from outside the file.

.github/workflows/test.yml.seam: CI triggers: run the unit and e2e matrix on push to Kilo's `v2` integration branch (upstream's v2 line is `dev`). Skip the `affected` job, and with it the `e2e-suite` jobs that need it and the `e2e` result check that requires `affected` to succeed: they test only `packages/app` and `packages/session-ui`, which Kilo removed (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). Job-level lines, so upstream changes to the e2e steps still merge cleanly. `Build workspace libraries` in upstream's `build` job filters only on `@opencode/cli^...`, because turbo fails on the `@opencode/app^...` filter when the package does not exist. CI speed: `Verify packed workerd SDK` runs in its own `sdk` job (at the end of the file), so it no longer waits for the unit tests in `unit`. The Turbo cache step (upstream removed its broken one in v2.0.31) uses `.turbo/cache` (where Turborepo 2.x writes), keys on turbo.json and bun.lock, and carries the shard. Test shards: a `shard` matrix dimension in `unit` (2 Linux, 3 Windows) sets `KILO_TEST_SHARD` and `KILO_TEST_CONCURRENCY`; core, tui and cli run `test:ci` (the Kilo runner, script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts); a `packages` leg per OS runs `test` once for the other packages, and on Linux the Effect, codemode, generated client and generated documentation checks, in parallel with the shards (they ran before the shard 1 tests and on both Linux shards, which made shard 1 the slowest job); failing cases from the runner's JUnit reports become annotations, and the reports are an artifact that refreshes the shard weights. No seam: workflow triggers, job conditions, jobs, steps, matrix dimensions and cache keys cannot be extended from outside the file. Upstream has no cache key input or test shard option.

.gitignore.seam: Ignore the v1 line's local dev profile (`.kilo-dev/`, left behind when one checkout switches between `main` and `v2`), `telemetry-id`, generated dependency installs, merge reports, and JetBrains state under `.kilo/`, and `packages/app/.artifacts/`. No seam: root gitignore rules cannot live in a Kilo-owned file. The v2 `bun dev` profile moved into the Kilo host package (packages/kilo-cli/.gitignore, U-E0-01); the remaining patterns are not host entries and stay. Reconciled by 3-way merge during upstream syncs.
.gitignore.unmarked: Eleven ignore patterns. A gitignore pattern line cannot carry an inline comment, so each pattern is preceded by a `# kilocode_change:` comment line.

AGENTS.md.seam: One marked block at the top with the Kilo rules for the v2 line (integration branch `origin/v2`, moving base, branch names, `bun dev` isolation instead of `dev:live`, plugin-first placement, direction of code movement, checks), pointing at migration-context.md, the plan, the fork conventions and the skills. It overrides the upstream rules it contradicts (default branch `dev`, `dev:live` against the installed service). Instructions only, no behavior. No seam: `AGENTS.md` is the only root instruction file that every agent used on this repository reads (v2 core loads only `AGENTS.md`, `core/src/config/plugin/instruction.ts`). A Kilo `instructions` entry in a root `kilo.json` would reach Kilo sessions only, and the contradicting upstream rules would still be in this file, so the override sits next to them. The upstream text below the block stays untouched, so syncs conflict only when upstream edits the first lines.

CONTRIBUTING.md.seam: Development setup names the exact Bun version from `packageManager` (3 lines). Documentation for contributors of this repository; `bun run build` and `install:alpha` fail on another Bun version. No seam: the contributor guide is a single upstream-owned file and has no Kilo-owned equivalent that GitHub shows. Goes away when the Kilo docs replace CONTRIBUTING.md.

README.md.seam: Show the generated Kilo v2 migration progress map (badge, treemap, history from migration-tracking/progress/) on the branch front page. Visibility only, no behavior. No seam: the repository README is a single upstream-owned file, and a Kilo-owned README cannot be the front page of the same repository. The Kilo host (U-E0-01) is a package and does not change the front page. Goes away when the map is published outside the repository (for example GitHub Pages).

package.json.seam: Root `dev` script runs script/dev-isolated.ts, which starts the Kilo host entry (packages/kilo-cli) with an isolated profile, so `bun dev` never uses the installed OpenCode or Kilo data. Stays after U-E0-01: `bun dev` from the root reads the upstream root package.json, and upstream's script runs the upstream CLI with the real data. Root `lint` script runs only `oxlint`: its ast-grep and `script/sdk-docs.ts` steps check `packages/gui-extensions`, which Kilo removed (`skipFiles`). Root `install:alpha` script runs script/kilocode/install-alpha.ts (Kilo-owned), which installs the host executable built by the `kilo-v2` workflow; it goes away when v2 is mainline.

packages/cli/package.json.seam: Export `./*` (`./src/*.ts`) as `core`, `server` and `util` do, so the Kilo host (packages/kilo-cli, U-E0-01) can run the upstream command handlers and services. Generic: any embedding entry can use it. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the CLI exported only `./run` and `./server-process`, so no entry outside the package could reach `Commands`, `Runtime` or a handler. Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/cli/script/app-assets.ts.seam: Build an empty web UI archive when `packages/app` does not exist, because Kilo removed it (`skipFiles` in script/upstream/utils/config.ts). One generic condition covers the release build (`build.ts`) and the Node build (`build-node.ts`). The server then answers non-API paths with 404, as on v1. No seam: the build scripts call `buildAppArchive` directly.

packages/cli/script/service-smoke.ts.seam: Accept a 404 for the web UI shell in the compiled service smoke test, because the Kilo build embeds no web UI (`packages/app` removed). The API, authentication, and plugin checks still run. No seam: the smoke script has no option to skip the web UI check.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/mcp/a.seam: Kilo config write target for `mcp add` (feature `config`): the first existing file of `.kilo2/kilo2.jsonc`, `.kilo2/kilo2.json`, `kilo2.jsonc`, `kilo2.json`, else `kilo2.json`; the global directory checks only its root files. Internal releases use kilo2 names without a v1 fallback (decision 12); the file order follows v1. Rung 4: the handler imports a Kilo module (util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts, which holds the names and order) and calls out to it. No seam: the CLI never builds Core `Config` and may not import Core (`test/import-boundaries.test.ts`), so the discovery layout node does not reach it, and Kilo's write order (directory before root files, `.jsonc` first, global root-only) differs in shape from upstream's, so a generic knob would be Kilo-shaped. The call-out is unconditional, so the upstream `packages/cli` binary (not shipped) also writes `kilo2.json` while its server reads only `opencode.*`.

packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/plugi.seam: Kilo config path for `plugin add` and `plugin remove` (feature `config`): pass global mode to `resolveConfigPath` (mcp/add.ts) so the global directory checks only its root files, like Kilo v1. Rung 4: one marked line each; the order lives in util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts. No hook, node or option for the config path in the CLI handlers.

Kilo config path for `plugin add` and `plugin remove` (feature `config`): pass global mode to `resolveConfigPath` (mcp/add.ts) so the global directory checks only its root files, like Kilo v1. Rung 4: one marked line each; the order lives in util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts. No hook, node or option for the config path in the CLI handlers.

packages/cli/src/server-process.ts.seam: `Options.overrides` (service replacements), passed through to `ServerProcess.start` in packages/server/src/process.ts, so an embedding entry's `serve` handler can replace services in the server it starts. The Kilo host registers the Kilo plugins this way (`SdkPlugins.node` replacement, U-E0-01). Two lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: `run` built the server options itself and had no way to add a replacement.

packages/core/package.json.seam: Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/core/src/config.ts.seam: Config discovery layout (feature `config`): `ConfigDiscovery.LayoutService`, a global node with upstream defaults (`opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode`, no walk bound) that discovery and `Config` read for the root file names, the project directory names, the file order inside those directories, the upward-walk bound and the global write target (the last existing name). Optional systemFiles and parse hooks let a host select managed file order and decode its own config schema from raw and normalized fields; the decoder also preserves host fields when managed policies split from settings. Generic: no Kilo name, import or condition; without the hooks, the default graph and canonical schema behave as upstream. The Kilo host supplies kilo2 names, v1 file orders, a worktree boundary and the Kilo-owned hide_prompt_training_models schema. Internal releases have no v1 filename fallback (decision 12). Rungs 1 and 2 cannot do it alone: config discovery and parsing run before plugins load, and replacing Config.node would lose the server's configured options.

packages/core/src/config/discovery.ts.seam: Config discovery layout (feature `config`): `ConfigDiscovery.LayoutService`, a global node with upstream defaults (`opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode`, no walk bound). Optional systemDirectory, systemFiles and parse hooks let a host select platform managed directories and file order and decode its own config schema. A decoder may report field diagnostics through the existing source-aware normalization warning pipeline, retaining valid fields instead of silently dropping an extension setting or the whole document. Explicit system options keep priority and existing macOS ai.opencode.managed preferences are unchanged. Generic: no Kilo name, import or condition; without the hooks, discovery and parsing behave as upstream. The Kilo host supplies kilo2 names, v1 file orders, the worktree boundary, /etc/kilo, /Library/Application Support/kilo, ProgramData/kilo and its Kilo-owned config schema. Tests inject a directory through explicit system options or the layout, not an ambient test environment override. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot do it alone: discovery and parsing run before plugins load, and replacing Config.node would lose the server's configured options.

packages/core/src/plugin/sdk.ts.seam: Registration phase for embedder plugins: `register(plugin, { phase: "post" })` and `all(phase)`. Without a phase, `all()` returns what it returned before. The Kilo agents use it: the agent ceiling must run after `ConfigAgentPlugin`, which is an internal post plugin (U-E2-12). Six lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the store had no phase, so every embedder plugin ran before the internal post plugins and a plugin could not act on the result of config.

packages/core/src/plugin/internal.ts.seam: Expose the existing Location-service provider to embedder plugins. The supervisor applies it without changing pre/post order or upstream defaults. Required for account config and managed policy reads at plugin activation; the public plugin context has no config domain, and host-global registration cannot supply a Location-scoped Config service. All feature logic stays in Kilo-owned plugins.

packages/core/src/plugin/supervisor.ts.seam: Appends the embedder plugins registered with phase `post` (`SdkPlugins.all("post")`) after the internal post plugins, so they see the result of config. Provides the existing Location-service context to embedder plugins in both phases, as internal plugins already receive it. No boot-order or upstream default change. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the supervisor builds the boot order itself, and host-global registration cannot supply Location-scoped services such as Config.

packages/server/src/process.ts.seam: `ServerProcess.start` takes `overrides` (service replacements) and passes them to `createRoutes`, which already takes them (as `ServerFetch.BootOptions.overrides` does for the embedded server). Three lines, no Kilo value. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot supply it: the process server built its routes without replacements, so a host could not register plugins (`SdkPlugins`) or replace services in the server the CLI spawns.

packages/tui/package.json.seam: Add a `test:ci` script that runs the Kilo test runner (script/kilocode/test/test-runner.ts) in balanced shards for CI. Turborepo runs only package.json scripts, so the sharded task needs a script in each sharded package (core, tui, cli); the package's own `test` script stays as it is and the runner calls it with file arguments.

packages/tui/src/component/dialog-integr.seam: Prompt for Personal Account vs Team (`chooseKiloAccount`) after a Kilo Gateway login completes, before closing or chaining the integration dialog. `TuiPlugin` has no post-integration-connect hook. The connect dialog also ranks and groups integrations with Kilo's v1 provider priority (`KILO_INTEGRATION_PRIORITY` in tui/src/kilocode/gateway.tsx: Kilo first under Popular, OpenCode Go and OpenCode Console under Services). `integrationOptions` takes the priority map as a parameter with upstream's map as the default (generic seam, so upstream's integration-options tests pass unchanged), and the dialog passes the Kilo map and uses it for the Popular group (rung 4). The map is a constant in the TUI process: no TUI plugin hook ranks integrations, and the host runs in the server process.

packages/tui/src/component/dialog-model..seam: Model picker (U-E9-07, #15242): the connected picker returns the Kilo option list (Kilo Gateway order from `recommendedIndex`, Recommended and Kilo Gateway sections, `Free` from Gateway `isFree`, `BYOK` and `May train` labels, v1 search over provider and model IDs) from the first line of its options memo, keeps section headers while searching (`flat={false}`), follows the highlight with `onMove`, and wraps the list with the model info panel. Seven call-out lines; the logic is in tui/src/kilocode/dialog-model.tsx and tui/src/kilocode/model-picker.ts. The upstream option code below the early return, `sortModelOptions` and `prioritizeFavorites` stay unchanged, so upstream syncs merge cleanly and upstream's model-options tests pass. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot reach it: the TUI plugin API has no model picker hook, and the host runs in the server process. A generic seam (an option-list and side-panel hook) would need the same lines here plus a new plugin API surface for one consumer.

packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx.seam: Full TUI default selection (Gateway): call the Kilo-owned default-model loader, then use SDK model.default after CLI/config and recent models, within the existing user/agent selection precedence. Keep the first catalog model when the server supplies no valid default. Without a higher-priority selection, catalog readiness waits for the default request so --prompt cannot submit the catalog's first model before the recommendation arrives. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot reach LocalProvider's private fallback memo or readiness flag; the TUI plugin API has no model-default resolver, and the host runs in the server process. A generic seam would add a resolver registration API for this single SDK read instead of these small call-outs. Loading, refresh and location isolation stay in tui/src/kilocode/default-model.ts.

packages/plugin/src/tui/context.ts.seam: Declare the `home.bottom` slot path in the public `SlotMap`, so a TUI plugin can render below the home prompt, as the v1 `home_bottom` slot allowed (Kilo Gateway news uses it). The v2 home screen publishes only `home.footer` and `home.footer.status`; a `before`/`after` claim on those places content at the bottom of the screen, not below the prompt. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot add a slot path: `SlotMap` is the closed public type of the plugin API. One generic line with no Kilo value.

packages/tui/src/routes/home.tsx.seam: Render the `home.bottom` plugin slot directly below the home prompt (the v1 `home_bottom` position). Without a claim it renders nothing, so the upstream home screen is unchanged. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot add a slot boundary to the home route. One generic line with no Kilo value; the Kilo news banner lives in tui/src/kilocode/kilo-news.tsx.

packages/tui/src/plugin/builtins.ts.seam: Register the built-in `KiloTeams` TUI plugin (`/teams`, `/team`, `/org`, `/orgs`), the `KiloNews` TUI plugin (Kilo Gateway news on the home screen) and the `KiloUsage` TUI plugin (`/usage`, `/plans`, `/quota`). Stays after U-E0-01: the TUI loads its built-in list in the TUI process, which `SdkPlugins` (a server store) does not reach. The config-driven path (`plugins` in the TUI config, loaded by `tui/src/plugin/context.tsx`) loads only npm packages or local files, which a compiled binary does not have. A generic seam needs an `@opencode/tui` export of the list (package.json) plus an extension point in this file, which is not fewer shared lines than these two.

packages/tui/test/fixture/local.tsx.seam: Wait for model catalog readiness in the shared LocalProvider test fixture, now that its last fallback includes an asynchronous SDK default. Existing test assertions stay unchanged. The optional waitForDefault flag lets Kilo-owned tests hold that request pending to check startup and location races. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot extend the fixture's private initialization sequence.

packages/tui/test/fixture/tui-client.ts.seam: Neutral SDK model.default response for the shared HTTP test fixture: no model data, so upstream selection assertions keep testing their original first-model fallback. The full TUI now reads this existing API to obtain the host's recommendation. No Kilo model or assertion change. Rungs 1 and 2 cannot extend the fixture's closed route dispatcher; without this route Bun.serve reports its unexpected-request throw before the client's fallback can handle the failed request. The same applies to plugin RPC calls (`/api/rpc/*`) from built-in TUI plugins such as the Kilo news banner: the fixture answers them as unregistered (404) so the plugin's failure path runs and upstream screens stay unchanged; Kilo-owned tests serve their own RPC answers.

packages/util/src/global.ts.seam: The app directory name under the XDG bases (`const app`) reads `OPENCODE_APP_DIR_NAME` and defaults to `opencode`, so an embedding entry can name its own config, data, cache, state and tmp directories. The Kilo host sets `kilo2` in packages/kilo-cli/src/env.ts before any upstream module loads (U-E1-01 part 1, D-4). One line, no Kilo value. Rung 2 cannot supply it: `Global.layerWith` replaces only the service in one graph, while `Global.Path` and `Flock.setGlobal({ state })` are computed when this module loads and read statically by the log file (util/observability/logging.ts), the server tmp (server/src/process.ts) and the TUI themes (tui/src/mini/theme.ts); `cli/src/server-process.ts` and `cli/src/commands/handlers/default.ts` compile their own `Global` node from those defaults, so the background service and the database stayed under `opencode` with host composition alone (measured: the service read its port from `~/.config/opencode` and logged to `~/.local/share/opencode/log`).

turbo.json.seam: Define `@opencode/core#test:ci`, `@opencode/tui#test:ci` and `@opencode/cli#test:ci` (a generic `test:ci` task adds a no-op node to every package): `dependsOn: ["transit"]` like upstream's generic `test`, `env: ["KILO_TEST_SHARD"]` gives each shard its own cache key, `passThroughEnv` hands the runner its concurrency and deadline, and `inputs` add the runner and its durations from script/kilocode/test/. Upstream has no sharded test task. The `transit` task and the `@kilocode/gateway-core#test` entry that Kilo carried are upstream since v2.0.32 (generic `test` on `transit`, anomalyco/opencode#55866 and anomalyco/opencode#56117).

packages/cli/src/services/updater.ts.seam: Kilo config names for the autoupdate policy (feature `config`): read the `update` or legacy `autoupdate` key from Kilo's global config names (`kilo2.json`, `kilo2.jsonc`, last defined policy wins) instead of `config.json`/`opencode.json(c)` or v1 `kilo.json(c)`. Internal releases have no v1 filename fallback (decision 12). Rung 4: one import and one marked line in an upstream CLI service; the CLI may not import Core (`test/import-boundaries.test.ts`), so it calls out to `util/src/kilocode/config/files.ts`. No hook or node for the updater policy.

packages/core/src/session/usage.ts.seam: The static SessionUsage function has no plugin hook or replaceable service for provider-reported billing. Its optional provider ID invokes Kilo-owned session/usage.ts before unchanged token pricing; callers that omit it retain upstream behavior. A new generic billing framework would require a larger API than this call-out.

packages/core/src/session/runner/publish.seam: The publisher discards raw usage after normalization and no public response-finish hook can amend the settlement. Pass the Kilo-owned cost and minimal response identity into the existing step record/native fields, without adding durable events or projections.

packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts.seam: Step settlement has no hook or replaceable service between the publisher record and Step.Ended/Failed. Prefer the optional provider charge from the existing finish record, including zero, before unchanged catalog pricing. Policy is in the Kilo-owned usage module.

packages/core/src/session/title.ts.seam: Title usage calls the static SessionUsage.record function outside primary step settlement. Pass the already selected provider ID to the same Kilo-owned billing policy; no title-spend hook or service override exists.

packages/core/src/session/compaction.ts.seam: Native and streamed compaction settle their usage through static SessionUsage.record outside the step runner. Pass the selected provider ID to the same Kilo-owned policy. A compaction transform replaces the operation, not these settlement calls, and would duplicate upstream compaction.

packages/core/src/session/stats.ts.seam: Statistics construct their grouping SQL locally with no model-identity hook or service override. One Kilo-owned SQL expression reads the durable actual route for Kilo steps and keeps the requested model fallback and all non-Kilo grouping unchanged.

packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.ts.seam: The production transcript has no plugin renderer slot for assistant footers, token usage rows, or intermediate step labels. Narrow call-outs render Kilo-owned actual-route components while preserving requested Auto identity and upstream rendering.

packages/tui/src/routes/session/group-vi.seam: Collapsed reasoning, exploration, and activity groups do not expose a plugin label slot. A Kilo-owned badge reads each group's assistant identities so hidden reasoning/tool steps do not lose their routes.

packages/tui/src/util/session.ts.seam: The static context-usage resolver has no plugin hook. A Kilo-owned actual-model lookup supplies the served model's context limit when available, with the original requested model lookup as fallback.

packages/tui/src/ui/dialog-select.tsx.seam: Keep the list footer mounted when its action list becomes empty. The footer is wrapped in a Show that unmounts it whenever no action is visible, and each mount registers a renderer resize listener through useTerminalDimensions. Selection changes that hide or show an action (for example the account row in the Kilo gateway dialog) therefore add listeners until the renderer exceeds its budget and writes a MaxListenersExceededWarning over the TUI. Rungs 1 to 3 cannot reach it: the footer is rendered by upstream's DialogSelect, and no plugin hook or generic knob controls whether that element stays mounted. Separately (rung 3 lines, no Kilo value): match the active row by option reference instead of by value (`active`, mouse move and mouse down, the scroll-to-top check), as on v1. A list may show one value twice: the model picker keeps a recent model in Recent and in its provider section (v1 placement). With value equality both copies render active and the pointer targets the first copy. For lists with unique values the behavior is the same, so upstream's DialogSelect tests pass. No plugin hook or host option reaches DialogSelect's private row matching.
